about.legal:
1. Purpose and authorization

UnattendLocal prepares Windows installation answer files locally. Use it only for devices and data you own or are explicitly authorized to manage. Rights to use Windows, software, keys and installation media are determined by their respective owners. This tool does not provide Windows activation rights or replace software licenses.

2. Installation, disks and scripts

Generating or exporting a file does not operate on the target disk. When used for installation, partitioning, formatting, app removal, policies and scripts act on the target system and may cause data loss or affect its operation. Back up important data, verify the target disks and partitions, and test in a virtual machine first. Custom scripts may operate beyond the scope shown in the summary. This tool does not execute these scripts on the current computer.

3. Credentials and file handling

Answer XML, Wi-Fi profiles, saved plans and custom scripts may contain account passwords, Wi-Fi passwords, product keys, tokens and other sensitive information. Base64 is reversible encoding, not encryption. The preview masks some recognized credentials; this does not mean that exported files, original content or custom scripts have been fully sanitized. Review all content before sharing.

Keeping installation-sensitive files controls the original generator's cleanup of specified files. It does not control deletion commands in custom scripts or remove originals from installation media. For preset local accounts, automatic cleanup currently requires the first automatic sign-in. If automatic sign-in is disabled, retention must be explicitly selected; the tool does not select it on your behalf.

4. Offline use and imported configuration

Editing, saving, generation and this explanation work offline. Downloads, Microsoft-account sign-in and other network scripts depend on the configuration and target installation environment. Unrecognized imported XML content is preserved where possible. Structural checks and previews are not a complete security or compatibility review. Use trusted sources and review the original content.

5. Upstream project and third-party licenses

The generation core comes from Christoph Schneegans's UnattendGenerator. UnattendLocal is an independent desktop interface and adaptation, not an official desktop release by the original author. Copyright notices, complete licenses and third-party information are available under Open-source licenses. The local interface and adaptation use the MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 tigerJX95. See LICENSE in the source and the project entry in the license page. Third-party components retain their own licenses and attribution. This explanation grants no additional trademark or other rights.

6. Responsibility and applicable law

Verify authorization, backups, targets and configuration. Compatibility and installation results depend on the Windows version, media, hardware, policies and scripts. The tool does not promise unattended completion in every environment. Responsibility is determined by applicable law and the circumstances. This explanation does not exclude or limit liability that cannot legally be excluded or limited, or require users to waive statutory rights.

v121.ntfs.help: No change by default. Sets the system-wide 8.3 name creation policy; does not remove existing names. Reboot may be required; legacy software might depend on short names.
v121.pagefile.help:
Leaves page-file settings unchanged by default. When enabled, configures initial and maximum sizes of C:\pagefile.sys in MiB during system setup, preserving page files on other drives.

Does not disable paging. A reboot may be required; choose sizes according to disk space, workload and crash-dump requirements.

v122.label.name: Set the system volume label
v122.label.purpose: Rename the installed Windows system volume, for example to Windows, without formatting or repartitioning.
v122.label.requirements:
Runs during System and resolves the installed Windows system drive automatically.

Edit $label to change the default Windows label. Requires NTFS and a non-empty label of at most 32 characters without path or control characters. Added disabled; review before enabling.

v122.power.purpose: Create and activate an Ultimate Performance power plan for sustained-performance workloads; energy use and heat may increase.

Reuses its own plan on repeat runs and stops if that GUID belongs to another plan. Support depends on Windows and hardware; unsupported systems report an error without a fallback. This later script overrides a selected Preferred power plan, so choose only one configuration method. Added disabled.
v123.firewall.name: Advanced diagnostics: firewall dropped-packet logging
v123.firewall.purpose: Enable local dropped-packet logging for Domain, Private and Public firewall profiles to troubleshoot connectivity.
v123.firewall.requirements:
Runs during System and configures logging in the local PersistentStore. The default maximum log size is 16384 KiB; edit to a value from 1 to 32767 KiB.

Preserves existing log paths and allowed-connection logging. Does not change firewall state, rules or inbound/outbound defaults. Organization policy may override effective settings. Disabling the template does not undo a previous deployment. Added disabled.

v123.winget.purpose: Install an explicitly selected package ID for online deployment; see usage examples for individual applications.
v123.winget.requirements:
Runs during FirstLogon on Windows 11 24H2 or later with an administrator, network access and App Installer. Set PackageId at the top of the script; an empty value stops execution.

Waits up to 300 seconds for WinGet, uses an exact ID from the winget source and machine-wide silent installation, without forced upgrades or hash bypass. v123.exe.purpose: Install an explicitly selected local EXE silently for offline deployment or prepared installation media.
v123.exe.requirements:
